G9701.definition: to fence by a palisade, fortify , (Aeschines Orator) (ML)

G9703.definition:
1. to make sharp  or pointed, sharpen, whet , (Hesiod) 
2. to furnish with notches  or teeth , like a saw, (Aristotle Philosopher):—;Pass., σκύταλον κεχ. ὄζοις a staff jagged  or rugged  with branches, (Theocritus Poeta Bucolicus): metaphorically, [ ὄμμα] ἠλεμάτοις ἀκτῖσι χαράσσεται sparkles  with false lights, of the effect produced by painting the eye-lids, [variant datesAnthology Palantina 
3. metaphorically in Pass., κεχαραγμένος τινί exasperated at  any one, (Herdotus Historicus); κείνῳ τόδε μὴ χαράσσου be not angry at  him for  this, (Euripides) 
4. to cut into furrows, cut, scratch , (Pindar):—;Pass., κέκοπται καὶ χαράσσεται πέδον (Aeschulus Tragicus) 
5. to engrave, inscribe , [Refs 3rd c.BC, variant datesAnthology Palantina (ML)

G9704.definition:
1. a joy , (Euripides); plural joys, delights , (Euripides) 
2. = χάρμα II, joy, delight , (Sophocles Tragicus) (ML)

G9710.definition:
1. of  or in winter, of  or in winter-time , opposite to θερινός, χ. τροπαί (see. τροπή 1), (Herdotus Historicus), etc.; τὴν χ. (i.e. ὥρην); during the winter season , (Herdotus Historicus) 
2. wintry , (Thucydides); see. χειμέριος. (ML)

G9712.definition:
1. a voting  or electing by show of hands , (Thucydides) 
2. a vote , Lat. suffragium, in plural, (Aeschines Orator) (ML)

G9713.definition:
1. to bring into hand, to manage, master, subdue , (Aristophanes Comicus) 
2. mostly in Mid., to conquer, overpower, subdue , (Herdotus Historicus); so, τήνδ᾽ ἐχειρούμην ἄγραν became master of  this booty, (Sophocles Tragicus) 
3. without any sense of violence, to master, subdue , (Xenophon Historicus), etc. 
4. χειροῦμαι is also Pass. to be subdued , [variant datesTragica Adespota; future χειρωθήσομαι (Demosthenes Orator); aor1 ἐχειρώθην (Herdotus Historicus); perfect κεχείρωμαι (Aeschulus Tragicus) (ML)

G9714.definition:
1. the swallow , (Odyssey by Homer), etc.:—; the twittering of the swallow was proverbially used of barbarous tongues by the Greeks, (Aeschulus Tragicus); χελιδόνων μουσεῖα (see. μουσεῖον);  proverbs also, μία χελιδὼν ἔαρ οὐ ποιεῖ (Aristotle Philosopher) 
2. the frog in a horse's foot , so called from its being forked like the swallow's tail , (Xenophon Historicus) (ML)

G9715.definition:
1. a tortoise , (Homeric Hymns); prov. of insensibility, ἰὼ χελῶναι μακάριαι τοῦ δέρματος oh ye tortoises , happy in your thick skins! (Aristophanes Comicus) 
2. like Roman testudo, a pent-house formed of shields overlapping each other like the scales on a tortoise's back , used by storming parties in approaching a city's walls: then, generally, a pent-house  for protecting besiegers, (Xenophon Historicus) (ML)

G9718.definition: on  or of dry land , ὄρνιθες χ. land- birds, opposite to λιμναῖοι, (Herdotus Historicus); χ. κροκόδειλος a lizard, (Herdotus Historicus):—;also of landsmen , as opposite to seamen, (Euripides); κῦμα χερσαῖον στρατοῦ, an army, opposite to a fleet, (Aeschulus Tragicus) (ML)

G9719.definition:
1. dry land, land , ἐπὶ χέρσου, opposite to ἐν πόντῳ, (Odyssey by Homer); κύματα κυλινδόμενα προτὶ χέρσον (Odyssey by Homer); κῦμα χέρσῳ ῥηγνύμενον (Iliad by Homer); χέρσῳ on  or by land , (Aeschulus Tragicus) 
2. as adjective, χέρσος, ον, dry, firm , of land, (Herdotus Historicus); ἐν κονίᾳ χέρσῳ, opposite to πόντῳ, (Pindar) 
3. dry, hard, barren , (Herdotus Historicus); χ. λιμήν a harbour left dry , [variant datesAnthology Palantina 
4. metaphorically barren, without children , of women, (Sophocles Tragicus): with genitive barren of , πυρὰ χέρσος ἀγλαϊσμάτων (Euripides) 
Prob. from same Root as ξηρός. (ML)

G9721.definition:
1. Radic. sense, to pour : 
2. properly of liquids, to pour out, pour , (Homer), etc.; Zeus χέει ὕδωρ, i. e. he makes it rain, (Iliad by Homer); χέει χιόνα βορέας (Euripides); absolute, χέει it snows , (Iliad by Homer):—;Mid. to pour for oneself , especially of drink-offerings, χοὰς χεόμην νεκύεσσι (Odyssey by Homer), etc.:—;Pass., χέονται κρῆναι they gush forth , (Euripides); χυθέντος ποτοῦ ἐς γῆν (Sophocles Tragicus) 
3. χ. δάκρυα to shed  tears, (Iliad by Homer):—;Pass., of tears, to pour  or gush forth , (Homer); so of blood, to be shed , (Aeschulus Tragicus) 
4. in Pass. to become liquid, melt, thaw , (Xenophon Historicus) 
5. of solids, to shed, scatter , φύλλα (Iliad by Homer); πτερά (Odyssey by Homer); χ. κόνιν κὰκ κεφαλῆς (Homer); χ. καλάμην χθονί, of a mower or reaper (see. καλάμη), (Iliad by Homer) 
6. like χώννυμι, to throw out  earth, so as to form a mound, σῆμα, τύμβον χ. (Homer) 
7. χ. δοῦρα to pour  or shower  spears, (Iliad by Homer); Mid., βέλεα χέοντο they showered their  arrows, (Iliad by Homer) 
8. to let fall  or drop , ἡνία (Iliad by Homer); so, χέειν κρόκου βαφὰς (see. βαφή II) (Aeschulus Tragicus); but, καρπὸν χ., of trees, to produce  fruit abundantly , (Odyssey by Homer) 
9. in Pass. to be thrown  or heaped up together , (Homer) 
10. in Pass. also of living beings, to pour  or stream in a dense mass  or throng , (Homer) 
11. metaphorically of sounds, to pour forth , φωνήν, αὐδήν (Odyssey by Homer); φθόγγον (Aeschulus Tragicus) 
12. of things that obscure the sight, κατ᾽ ὀφθαλμῶν χέεν ἀχλύν shed  a dark cloud over the eyes, (Iliad by Homer); πολλὴν ἠέρα χεῦε shed  a mist abroad, (Odyssey by Homer):—;Pass., ἀμφὶ δέ οἱ θάνατος χύτο was shed  around him, (Iliad by Homer); νόσος κέχυται (Sophocles Tragicus); φρὶξ ἐπὶ πόντον ἐχεύατο (Mid. in passive sense), (Iliad by Homer) 
13. of persons, ἀμφ᾽ αὐτῶι χυμένη throwing herself  around him, (Homer): so in Mid., ἀμφὶ υἱὸν ἐχεύατο πήχεε (Iliad by Homer) 
14. perfect passive κέχυμαι, to be wholly engaged in , Δᾶλος, ἐν ἇι κέχυμαι (Pindar) (ML)

G9722.definition:
1. a horse's hoof , (Hesiod):—;also, a cloven hoof , (Euripides) 
2. in plural, of the talons  of a bird, [variant datesTragica Adespota; of a wolf's claws , (Theocritus Poeta Bucolicus) 
3. a sea-bank, breakwater , formed of stones laid at the base of a sea-wall, to break the force of the waves (so called because it projected like a hoof) , Lat. crepido, (Thucydides) 
4. the spur of a mountain  or ridge of rocks  answering a like purpose, (Thucydides) 
5. a cloven implement , such as a netting-needle;—;  compare χηλεύω. (ML)

G9725.definition:
1. intransitive to be bereaved  of a person or thing, with genitive, (Odyssey by Homer) 
2. absolute to be bereaved of a husband, to be widowed, live in widowhood , (Demosthenes Orator), etc.;—;of a man, to be a widower , (Plutarch); so, χηρεύσει λέχος (Euripides) 
3. to live in solitude , of an exile, (Sophocles Tragicus) 
4. transitive to bereave , (Euripides) (ML)

G9726.definition: of yesterday , τὸ χθιζὸν χρεῖος their yesterday's  debt, (Iliad by Homer); ὁ χθ. πόνος yesterday's  labour, (Herdotus Historicus); in adverbial sense, with Verbs, χθιζὸς ἔβη he went yesterday , (Iliad by Homer); χθ. ἤλυθες (Odyssey by Homer), etc.:—;neuter χθιζόν as adverb = χθές, (Homer); so plural χθιζά, see. πρώιζος. (ML)

G9727.definition:
1. the earth, ground , (Homer); χθόνα δῦναι to go beneath the earth , i. e. to die, (Iliad by Homer); κατὰ χθονὸς κρύπτειν τινά (Sophocles Tragicus); κούφα σοι χθὼν ἐπάνω πέσοι (Euripides) 
2. of the nether world , οἱ ὑπὸ χθονός, i. e. those in the shades below , Lat. inferi, (Aeschulus Tragicus); κατὰ χθονὸς θεαί, i. e. the Erinyes, (Aeschulus Tragicus) 
3. earth , i. e. the whole earth, the world , (Aeschulus Tragicus) 
4. Earth , as a goddess, (Aeschulus Tragicus) 
5. a particular land  or country , of Ithaca, (Odyssey by Homer); of Libya, (Pindar); χθὼν Ἀσιᾶτις, Δωρίς, Ἀργεία, Ἑλλάς, Ἰδαία, etc., [variant datesTragica Adespota (ML)

G9728.definition: unripe wheaten groats , as ἄλφιτα are barley-groats, (Aristophanes Comicus) (ML)

G9729.definition:
1. the office  or post  of χιλίαρχος, (Xenophon Historicus) 
2. the office of the tribuni militares , (Xenophon Historicus) (ML)

G9732.definition:
1. a she-goat , Lat. capra, (Iliad by Homer), attic 
2. Χίμαιρα, ἡ, Chimaera , a firespouting-monster, with lion's head, serpent's tail, and goat's body, killed by Bellerophon, (Iliad by Homer) (ML)

G9733.definition:
1. a he-goat , Lat. caper, = τράγος, (Aristophanes Comicus) 
2. also feminine = χίμαιρα, [Refs 3rd c.BC, variant datesAnthology Palantina (ML)

G9735.definition:
Lat. laena, a large square upper-garment, a cloak, mantle, (Homer); it was made of wool, and worn over the χιτών, thrown over the shoulders, fastened with a pin or brooch  περόνη). It is also called φᾶρος by (Homer), and in later Greek ἱμάτιον, Latin pallium.  
derivation uncertain (ML)

G9741.definition:
1. any light porous substance , ἁλὸς χνόος the foam that gathers at the edge  of the sea, (Odyssey by Homer); πωλικὸς χν. horse's foam , [variant datesAnthology Palantina 
2. the first down on the chin  of youths, Lat. lanugo, (Aristophanes Comicus): the bloom  on fruit, [variant datesAnthology Palantina (ML)

G9744.definition:
1. like χόλη, gall, bile , (Iliad by Homer) 
2. generally metaphorically bile, gall, bitter anger, wrath , (Homer), attic; χόλος ἔδυ τινά (Iliad by Homer); χόλος ἔμπεσε θυμῷ (Iliad by Homer); χόλον πέσσειν, καταπέσσειν (see. entry); χ. σβέσσαι παῦσαι (Iliad by Homer); χόλου παύεσθαι (Hesiod):—;with genitive objecti, anger towards  or because of  another, (Iliad by Homer); with genitive rei, anger for, because of  a thing, (Sophocles Tragicus) 
3. an object of anger , [variant datesAnthology Palantina (ML)

G9746.definition:
1. gut-string, the string  of a lyre, Lat. chorda, (Odyssey by Homer) 
2. tripe , (Batrachomyomachia): also = χόρδευμα, (Aristophanes Comicus) (ML)

G9747.definition:
1. to dance a round  or choral dance , (Sophocles Tragicus), etc.; especially of the Bacchic chorus, (Euripides):—; to take part in the chorus , regarded as a matter of religion, (Sophocles Tragicus): to be one of a chorus , (Aristophanes Comicus): —;with dative pers. to dance to  him, in  his honour , (Euripides) 
2. generally, to dance , especially from joy, (Sophocles Tragicus) 
3. metaphorically to practise  a thing, be versed  in it, (Plato Philosophus) 
4. with accusative cognate, φροίμιον χορεύσομαι I will dance  a prelude (to festivities), (Aeschulus Tragicus); χ. γάμους to celebrate  them, (Euripides); ὄργια Μουσῶν (Aristophanes Comicus):—;Mid., χορεύεσθαι δίνας to ply the  eddying dance , (Euripides):—;Pass., κεχόρευται ἡμῖν (sings the Chorus) our part is played , (Aristophanes Comicus) 
5. transitive to celebrate in choral dance , Ἴακχον (Sophocles Tragicus):—;Pass. to be celebrated in choral dance , (Aristophanes Comicus) 
6. Causal, to set  one a dancing, to rouse, wake to the dance , τινά (Euripides); so, πόδα χορεύειν [variant datesAnthology Palantina (ML)

G9748.definition:
1. the office of a  χορηγός at Athens, the defraying of the cost of the public choruses , being the chief of the λειτουργίαι, (Thucydides), etc. 
2. means for providing  χοροί: abundance of means, fortune , (Aristotle Philosopher) 
3. metaphorically supplies for war , (Polybius Historicus) (ML)

G9749.definition: the membrane that encloses the fetus, the afterbirth , Lat. secundae: plural χόρια, ων, τά, a dish made by stuffing it with honey and milk , a kind of haggis , (Aristophanes Comicus): proverbial, χαλεπὸν χορίω (doric genitive) κύνα γεῦσαι "don't let a dog taste blood, " (Theocritus Poeta Bucolicus) (cf. Horace, canis a corio nunquam absterrebitur uncto).  (ML)

G9751.definition: a being fed, feasting , [variant datesAnthology Palantina (ML)

G9753.definition: a coos, a measurement of liquid (Lev.19.36)

G9754.definition:
to neigh, whinny , Lat. hinnire, of horses, (Iliad by Homer), etc. 
Formed from the sound. (ML)

G9756.definition:
1. that which one needs must pay, an obligation, debt , (Odyssey by Homer); a debt for stolen cattle , (Iliad by Homer); χρεῖος ἀποστήσασθαι to pay a debt  in full, (Iliad by Homer); ἀρᾶς τίνει χρ. pays the debt demanded by  the curse, (Aeschulus Tragicus); χρέος πόλει προσάπτειν to attach a further debt , i.e. guilt  to the city, (Sophocles Tragicus); χρέος ἀποδιδόναι to repay a debt , (Herdotus Historicus):—;in plural debts , χρειῶν λύσις (Hesiod); τὴν οὐσίαν ἅπασαν χρέα κατέλιπε left all the property in outstanding debts , (Demosthenes Orator) 
2. a needful business, an affair, matter , ἑὸν αὐτοῦ χρεῖος (Odyssey by Homer): a requirement, a purpose , (Sophocles Tragicus): with genitive, like χάριν, for the sake of , σὸν οὐκ ἔλασσον ἢ κείνης χρέος (Euripides) 
3. like χρῆμα, a thing , τί χρέο; = τί χρῆμ; wherefore?  (Aeschulus Tragicus); ἐφ᾽ ὅ τι χρ. ἐμόλετ; (Euripides) 
4. in (Odyssey by Homer), ἦλθον Τειρεσίαο κατὰ χρέος seems to be = Τειρεσίᾳ χρησόμενος, I came to consult  him:—;but, κατὰ χρέος according to what is due , as is meet , (Homeric Hymns) 
5. a duty, task, charge, office , (Pindar) (ML)

G9757.definition:
to utter oracles, divine , (Aristophanes Comicus) 
from χρησμολόγος (ML)

G9759.definition:
1. the surface of a body, the skin; the body  itself, (Iliad by Homer) 
2. the superficial appearance  of a thing, its colour , (Aeschulus Tragicus), etc.:—;especially the colour of the skin, the complexion , (Aeschulus Tragicus) (ML)

G9762.definition:
1. one who melts gold , of one who gilds the horns  of a victim, (Odyssey by Homer) 
2. a goldsmith , (Demosthenes Orator) (ML)

G9765.definition:
1. poured, shed , αἷμα χυτόν blood shed , (Aeschulus Tragicus) 
2. of dry things, shot out, heaped up , χυτὴ γαῖα a mound of  earth, a sepulchral mound, (Homer):—;as Substantive, χυτός, οῦ, = χῶμα, a mound, bank, dike , (Herdotus Historicus) 
3. melted , ἀρτήματα λίθινα χυτά pendants of melted  stone, (Herdotus Historicus) 
4. generally, liquid, flowing , [Refs 5th c.BC, variant datesAnthology Palantina (ML)

G9766.definition:
1. an earthen pot, a pot for boiling, pipkin , Lat. olla, (Aristophanes Comicus) 
2. χύτραι, pots of pulse  offered to inferior deities, (Aristophanes Comicus) (ML)

G9768.definition: a pot with feet , or a portable stove  for putting a pot upon, (Hesiod) (ML)

G9770.definition: to be  or go lame , (Plato Philosophus) (ML)

G9771.definition:
1. earth thrown up, a bank, mound , thrown up against the walls of cities to take them, (Herdotus Historicus):—; a dike  to hinder a river from overflowing, (Herdotus Historicus):—; a dam , (Herdotus Historicus):—; a mole  or pier , carried out into the sea, Lat. moles, (Herdotus Historicus) 
2. like Lat. tumulus, a sepulchral mound, [Refs 5th c.BC, variant datesTragica Adespota 
 
 (ML)

G9779.definition:
1. to cast into a mould (  χόανος), (Aristophanes Comicus) 
2. to cast metal: —;Pass., κεχωνευμένος (Plutarch) (ML)

G9782.definition:
1. a pair of scissors , Lat. forfex, [variant datesAnthology Palantina 
2. a building with a pointed stone roof, a vault , Lat. fornix, (Sophocles Tragicus) 
 
Deriv. unknown. (ML)

G9785.gloss: to sing along with stringed instruments
G9785.definition: to sing along with stringed instruments

G9787.definition: like a starling , i. e. speckled, dappled , ψ. ἵππος a dapple-gray  horse, (Aristophanes Comicus) (ML)

G9789.definition: to falter in speech, speak inarticulately :—;so in Mid., (Plato Philosophus) (ML)

G9793.definition: a proposition carried by vote : especially a measure passed in the  ἐκκλησία, a decree , (Aristophanes Comicus); τὸ Μεγαρέων ψ. the decree  concerning them, (Thucydides); so, περὶ Μεγαρέων ψ. (Thucydides); ψ. γράφειν to bring in a decree , (Aristophanes Comicus); ψ. ἐπιψηφίζειν, of the πρόεδροι, to put it  to the vote, (Aeschines Orator); ψ. νικᾶν to carry it , (Aeschines Orator); ψ. καθαιρεῖν to rescind it , Lat. abrogare, (Thucydides) (ML)

G9794.definition: to whisper, say into the ear , (Plato Philosophus):—;metaphorically, ὅταν πλάτανος πτελέᾳ ψιθυρίζῃ when the plane whispers  to the elm, (Aristophanes Comicus) (ML)

G9795.definition:
1. bare , 
2. of land, ψιλὴ ἄροσις a bare  corn-field, (Iliad by Homer); πεδίον μέγα τε καὶ ψιλόν (Herdotus Historicus): with genitive, γῆ ψιλὴ δενδρέων land bare  of trees, (Herdotus Historicus):—; ψιλὴ γεωργία the tillage of land for corn , opposite to γ. πεφυτευμένη (for vines  and olives) , (Aristotle Philosopher) 
3. of animals, stript of hair  or feathers, bare, smooth , δέρμα (Odyssey by Homer); ἶβις ψιλὴ κεφαλήν bald  on the head, (Herdotus Historicus) 
4. generally, bare, uncovered , ψιλὸν ὡς ὁρᾷ νέκυν (Sophocles Tragicus):—;with genitive bare of, separated from , ψιλὴ σώματος οὖσα [ ἡ ψυχή] (Plato Philosophus) b. bare, stript of appendages , ψιλὴ τρόπις the bare  keel with the planks torn from it, (Odyssey by Homer); ψ. θρίδαξ a lettuce with the side-leaves pulled off , (Herdotus Historicus); ψ. μάχαιραι swords without other arms , (Xenophon Historicus) 
5. οἱ ψιλοί (i.e. τῶν ὅπλων); soldiers without heavy armour, light troops , such as archers and slingers, opposite to ὁπλῖται, (Herdotus Historicus), etc.; τὸ ψιλόν, opposite to τὸ ὁπλιτικόν, (Xenophon Historicus); ψ. ἔχων τὴν κεφαλήν bare-headed, without helmet , (Xenophon Historicus) 
6. ψιλὸς λόγος bare  language, i. e. prose , as opposite to poetry which is clothed in metre, (Plato Philosophus); also, ψ. λόγος is a mere  speech, a speech unsupported by evidence , (Demosthenes Orator) 
7. ψιλὴ ποίησις mere  poetry, without music , i. e. epic  poetry, as opposite to lyric , (Plato Philosophus):—;but, ψιλὴ μουσική instrumental  music unaccompanied by the voice , (Aristotle Philosopher) 
8. Oedipus seems to call Antigone his ψιλὸν ὄμμα, as being the one poor  eye left him, (Sophocles Tragicus) 
9. adverb ψιλῶς, merely, only , (Plutarch) (ML)

G9796.definition:
1. to strip bare  of hair, (Herdotus Historicus):—; Pass. to become bald , (Hesiod): generally, to be laid bare , (Xenophon Historicus) 
2. with genitive to strip bare of, to strip of  a thing, (Herdotus Historicus) 
3. generally, to leave naked, unarmed  or defenceless , (Thucydides) 
4. Pass. also of things, to be stripped off  something, τὰ κρέα ἐψιλωμένα τῶν ὀστέων (Herdotus Historicus) (ML)

G9798.definition:
1. a blamable fault, a blemish, flaw , (Simonides Lyricus) 
2. blame, censure , (Pindar) (ML)

G9799.definition:
1. to make an inarticulate noise, to sound, make a noise , (Euripides); ψοφεῖ λάλον τι sounds chatter-like , as if it were tested like a pot, to see if it were cracked, (Aristophanes Comicus); ὥσπερ κύμβαλον ψοφεῖ (Xenophon Historicus) 
2. with accusative, ψοφεῖν τὰς θύρας to knock at  the door inside, to shew that some one was coming out, Menand.:—;also of the door (intransitive), εἰ αἱ θύραι νύκτωρ ψοφοῖεν, i. e. if they were heard to open , (Lysias Orator) (ML)
